Docs/Quick evaluation

Quick evaluation

Check environment wiring first, then run a learned checkpoint with a recorded seed manifest.

A small wiring test

From the SoftHandGrasping checkout, with the task assets and GR00T runtime dependencies installed:

python -m train.train_groot --evaluate --stub \
  --env-id SharpaAngledClickMouse-v1 \
  --control-mode pd_joint_pos --sim-backend physx_cpu \
  --camera-size 256 --num-eval-envs 1 \
  --num-eval-episodes 2 --num-eval-steps 20 \
  --max-episode-steps 500 --seed 10001
Not a benchmark score

The stub checks the environment/adapter loop. It does not load a learned policy or measure its success. These commands document the verified CLI arguments; the website does not execute simulator jobs.

Evaluate a checkpoint

python -m train.train_groot --evaluate \
  --env-id SharpaAngledClickMouse-v1 \
  --model-path /path/to/checkpoint \
  --control-mode pd_joint_pos --sim-backend physx_cpu \
  --camera-size 256 --num-eval-envs 1 \
  --num-eval-episodes 50 --num-eval-steps 500 \
  --max-episode-steps 500 --seed 10001 \
  --instruction-sampling canonical

This example uses the mouse stage’s 500-step horizon. For another task, use its registered profile; do not carry this horizon over to every stage.

Repeat across native scenes

Add --scene-background robocasa_l3_s2, then repeat with robocasa_l3_s1 and robocasa_l3_s6. Keep the checkpoint fixed and reuse the episode seeds. Preserve each run’s background manifest.
